\subsection{Filamentation}

Femtosecond laser pulse propagation in transparent dielectrics such as $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ can lead to the formation of \textbf{filaments}, which are self-guided light channels resulting from a dynamic balance between \textbf{Kerr self-focusing} and \textbf{plasma defocusing}. This phenomenon occurs when the input power exceeds a critical value, denoted as $P_{cr}$.

\subsubsection{Critical Power for Self-Focusing}
The critical power $P_{cr}$ is derived from the balance between the nonlinear self-focusing effect and diffraction. For a Gaussian beam, the critical power is given by:
\begin{equation}
    P_{cr} = \frac{3.77 \lambda_0^2}{8 \pi n_0 n_2},
\end{equation}
where $\lambda_0$ is the laser wavelength, $n_0$ is the linear refractive index, and $n_2$ is the nonlinear refractive index coefficient.

For fused silica, typical values are:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Linear refractive index: $n_0 \approx 1.45$ (at $\lambda_0 = 800 \text{ nm}$).
    \item Nonlinear refractive index: $n_2 \approx 2.7 \times 10^{-20} \text{ m}^2/\text{W}$ (at $\lambda_0 = 800 \text{ nm}$).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Calculation for $\mathrm{SiO}_2$}
Using the above values, we calculate $P_{cr}$ for two common wavelengths:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{For $\lambda_0 = 800 \text{ nm}$:}
    \begin{equation}
        P_{cr} = \frac{3.77 \times (800 \times 10^{-9})^2}{8 \pi \times 1.45 \times 2.7 \times 10^{-20}} \approx 2.5 \text{ MW}.
    \end{equation}

    \item \textbf{For $\lambda_0 = 1030 \text{ nm}$:}
    Assuming $n_2 \approx 2.2 \times 10^{-20} \text{ m}^2/\text{W}$ (slightly lower at longer wavelengths),
    \begin{equation}
        P_{cr} = \frac{3.77 \times (1030 \times 10^{-9})^2}{8 \pi \times 1.45 \times 2.2 \times 10^{-20}} \approx 4.1 \text{ MW}.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{Link to Intensity and PhysRevB.71.125435}
The critical power is related to the laser intensity $I$ through the beam area. For a Gaussian beam with radius $w_0$, the peak intensity is:
\begin{equation}
    I_0 = \frac{2 P}{\pi w_0^2}.
\end{equation}
Assuming a typical beam radius of $w_0 \approx 10 \text{ $\mu$m}$ (for tightly focused pulses as in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevB.71.125435}), the peak intensity for $P = P_{cr}$ is:
\begin{equation}
    I_0 \approx \frac{2 \times 2.5 \times 10^6}{\pi \times (10 \times 10^{-6})^2} \approx 1.6 \times 10^{13} \text{ W/cm}^2.
\end{equation}
This is consistent with the intensities around $5 \times 10^{13} \text{ W/cm}^2$ reported in Ref.~\cite{PhysRevB.71.125435}, where filamentation and damage tracks were observed. The discrepancy arises because filamentation can occur at powers \textbf{slightly above} $P_{cr}$, especially in the presence of plasma defocusing and other nonlinear effects.
